title: Getting the Nest Club job and playing for gangsters
summary: A phone call to the Bandbox sent him to the Nest, where drummer-leader George Howe and pianist Luis Russell hired him, and gangsters threw money after 3 a.m.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: At that time, I'm waiting for Chick to go to work, and I had just finished with (?)'s band. Now, here I'm standing in the Rhythm Club or the Bandbox, whatever you call it, and a phone call comes in for "Holmes, the saxophone player, don't forget to bring your horn around to the Nest Club." Well, the Nest was right around Thirty-Third Street, so it was right around the corner from the Bandbox -- two blocks, because the Bandbox was Thirty-First and the Nest was Thirty-Third Street.

Yeah. So, I always had my horn under my arm one way or another -- little raggedy bag. Always ready for the occasion, you know. Some of us used to wear tuxedos all day long. If we had a gig coming, we'd be all dressed!

So anyway, I go around there, and I tell them who I am. "My name is Charlie Holmes, saxophone. Somebody called here for a saxophone?" They said, "Oh yeah, yeah. Oh, you're Holmes, huh?" So I says, "Yeah." This little short guy was the drummer, and he was the leader. So he says; "All right, take your horn out." We was workin' now, you know. So I sit down in the band. I think Amos(?) was in that band...I think... You know, because everybody was giggin' with whoever you could.

So I sat down and got to blowing. And Russell was in the band, playing piano. And it happened I was sitting close to Russell. He said, "That sounds good. Sounds good to me." I said, "Thanks." You know, I don't know nothin' about none of these guys. They're all new to me. So George Howe, he looks over, comes around and shows his little self off. He says, "Do you want the job?" He said, "The job is open. It's yours if you want it." I said, "Okay. It's all right with me." So I taken the job. I wasn't doin' nothin'.

Taken the job, and you go to work from 10 o'clock to 11 o'clock at night, and get out there any time you could. That's when you got through. When the last customer leaves, then you can go home. Sometimes the last customer didn't leave until 10 o'clock in the morning -- and that's no joke. You can come out of there at 10 or 11 o'clock in the morning, and the sun be way high up in the sky.

See, because around about 3 o'clock all the other clubs would be closed, and then the gangsters would start falling in this place. And they could throw away some money. Them gangsters, they'd come in with their chicks and one thing or another, be throwin' money all over. All you had to do was know something that they liked, some music that they liked, and boy, they'd throw a hundred dollar bill up there in a
minute. Now, that ain't bad. Their take, you know.... Because when you walk up there and you've got your pockets full of money...
